summaryClaims.question: Initial intensity
summaryClaims.text: Assume the 2021 behavior: slow ground fire under a fallen tree from ~6:48 AM; ~600 to 800 sq ft by 4:30 PM; ~40 x 40 ft by 5:12 PM; ~2 acres by 5:42 PM; ~500 acres by 8 AM next day. No measured heat output on record.

summaryClaims.question: Aerial support
summaryClaims.text: Chico Regional Airport (~41 km W) is a CAL FIRE air attack and airtanker base; Aero-Flite also keeps a hangar there. Ag aviation operators in the Sacramento Valley (Chico, Biggs, Gridley, Colusa, Yuba City) can help only if carded and contracted as single engine air tankers; a Fire Boss version can scoop from large lakes. See Aircraft tab.

sourceText: Butte County, Chico Air Attack Base, https://www.buttecounty.ca.gov/563/Chico-Air-Attack-Base; Aerial Fire Magazine, Aero-Flite hangar in Chico (2024), https://aerialfiremag.com/2024/03/11/aero-flite-establishes-hangar-base-in-chico-california

summaryClaims.question: Cameras that could see it
summaryClaims.text: Bald Mtn. (Butte) 1 is 12 km away and was pointed at the origin when the list was read. Bald Mtn. La Porte 1 (40 km) also covers it. Bald Eagle Mtn. 1 (15 km) is 10 deg off with a narrow view. See Cameras tab. Terrain line of sight not checked.

summaryClaims.question: Could we detect it earlier?
summaryClaims.text: Likely yes, through the camera, but only with a camera-first mode (not built yet): today's pipeline only checks cameras near a satellite hotspot, so it would alert at the first GOES-18 detection (estimated evening), with the camera adding evidence. With camera-first mode, a WATCH could fire once smoke rises above the trees, plausibly hours before the 5:12 PM call. A power-outage source (PG&E public outage map) could flag the 6:48 AM fault. See Timeline tab.

sourceText: Firebender team estimate (not an official figure)
